summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic bowel obstruction, and line-associated DVTs was transferred to this hospital with altered mental status, bacteremia, and ileus. She had been confused for two days, attributed initially to missed magnesium and potassium supplements. Workup revealed polymicrobial bacteremia (Klebsiella pneumoniae, Enterococcus faecalis, and Staphylococcus epidermidis) from a femoral central line, acute toxic encephalopathy likely due to dehydration and metabolic stress, colonic ileus requiring NG tube decompression, and coagulopathy responsive to vitamin K. She was treated with intravenous antibiotics, later transitioned to oral linezolid and ciprofloxacin, bowel rest, and supportive care. Her mental status, bowel function, and labs improved. A midline catheter was placed for ongoing access. She developed iatrogenic peripheral edema from fluid resuscitation, managed conservatively. She was discharged home with oral antibiotics, increased potassium supplementation, a glucometer for monitoring, and plans for outpatient follow-up.
